title: Strict transform of an algebraic space as the blowup of the inverse-image ideal
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Open and closed immersions mean representable morphisms whose scheme base changes have the indicated property [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], with tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], write $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T$ for the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, constructed by etale descent of the ordinary scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] on affine etale charts. Finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections. An effective Cartier divisor is a closed subspace whose ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor. For a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$, a morphism $g:Y\to T$, and $p:T^{\prime}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T\to T$, the strict transform of $Y$ means the closed subspace of $Y\times_TT^{\prime}$ cut out by the ideal of sections locally annihilated by some power of a local equation of the exceptional effective Cartier divisor $p^{-1}V(\mathcal K)$. Here fibre products are those of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Put $\mathcal K\mathcal O_Y=\operatorname{im}(g^*\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_Y)$. There is a canonical isomorphism from $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K\mathcal O_Y}Y$ to this strict transform, commuting with the projections to $Y$ and $T^{\prime}$. In particular the canonical map $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K\mathcal O_Y}Y\to Y\times_TT^{\prime}$ is a closed immersion. Over $T\setminus V(\mathcal K)$ its projection to $T^{\prime}$ is the original morphism $g$ restricted to that open. If $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then $T^{\prime}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. If $g$ is separated and of finite type, then the strict-transform projection to $T^{\prime}$ is separated, of finite type, and quasi-separated (its relative diagonal is quasi-compact).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal J=\mathcal K\mathcal O_Y$, $B=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}Y$, and $P=Y\times_TT^{\prime}$. Tensor pullback preserves quasi-coherence and images of quasi-coherent maps are quasi-coherent by the cited module results. Locally, images of any finite generating list for $\mathcal K$ generate $\mathcal J$, so $\mathcal J$ is finite type. Thus the blowup chart-properties node applies both to $T^{\prime}\to T$ and to $b:B\to Y$: their extended centre ideals are effective Cartier ideals. In particular $\mathcal K\mathcal O_B=\mathcal J\mathcal O_B$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor. This equality follows directly by taking the ideal generated by images of local sections of $\mathcal K$ along the composite $B\to Y\to T$.

source.place: Tag 0864 (lemma-strict-transform), construction of the source blowup; Tag 085T (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor).

proof.text: On $P$, let $\mathcal H$ be the sheaf of exceptional power torsion. To check its construction, refine etale scheme charts until the exceptional ideal on $T^{\prime}$ has one equation $a$; on their pullbacks to $P$, the supported-kernel lemma identifies $\mathcal H$ with the quasi-coherent sheaf whose affine sections are $\Gamma_a(R)=\{r:\exists n,\ a^nr=0\}$. The Zariski--etale equivalence for quasi-coherent modules on schemes turns this Zariski submodule into a quasi-coherent submodule of $\mathcal O$ on the small etale site of the chart, with its scheme pullbacks matching the etale tensor pullbacks. Changes of etale scheme chart are flat on affine restrictions by the etale-algebra-flat node, so the same supported-kernel lemma identifies the pullback of this subsheaf with the corresponding subsheaf on the new chart. Replacing $a$ by a unit multiple leaves $\Gamma_a$ unchanged. These canonical submodule identifications satisfy the cocycle since all are inclusions in the structure sheaf. The cartesian-chart-family node therefore gives a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal O_P$. The ideal/closed-subspace correspondence constructs $i:W=V(\mathcal H)\hookrightarrow P$, exactly the strict transform in the statement, and gives its local ring $R/\Gamma_a(R)$.

Multiplication by $a$ on $R/\Gamma_a(R)$ is injective: if $ar\in\Gamma_a(R)$, then $a^{n+1}r=0$ for some $n$, whence $r\in\Gamma_a(R)$. The ideal $\mathcal J\mathcal O_W$ is generated on these charts by the image of $a$, since on $P$ the ideal generated by $\mathcal K$ is the pullback of its principal extended ideal on $T^{\prime}$. Thus $\mathcal J\mathcal O_W$ is an effective Cartier ideal. These assertions are local and require no injectivity for multiplication by $a$ on $R$ itself.

proof.text: The universal property of the blowup of $T$ now gives a unique $v:B\to T^{\prime}$ over $T$, since $\mathcal K\mathcal O_B$ is an effective Cartier ideal. Together with $b$ it gives $c:B\to P$. Every local section of $\mathcal H$ maps to zero on $B$: if $a^nr=0$, its image is killed by a power of the image of $a$, which is a non-zero-divisor because it generates $\mathcal K\mathcal O_B$. The closed-subspace factorization criterion gives a unique $\alpha:B\to W$ with $i\alpha=c$. Conversely the universal property of the blowup of $Y$ gives $\beta:W\to B$ over $Y$, since step 3 made $\mathcal J\mathcal O_W$ effective Cartier.

source.place: Tag 0864 (lemma-strict-transform), canonical map from the source blowup; Tag 085U (lemma-universal-property-blowing-up).

proof.text: The composite $\beta\alpha$ and $\mathrm{id}_B$ are both maps to $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}Y$ over $Y$, and $\mathcal J\mathcal O_B$ is effective Cartier. Uniqueness in that blowup universal property gives $\beta\alpha=\mathrm{id}_B$. To check the other composite, compare $i\alpha\beta=c\beta$ with $i$ as maps $W\to P=Y\times_TT^{\prime}$. Their $Y$-components coincide. Their $T^{\prime}$-components coincide by uniqueness in the blowup universal property over $T$, since $\mathcal K\mathcal O_W=\mathcal J\mathcal O_W$ is effective Cartier. The fibre-product universal property gives $i\alpha\beta=i$. A closed subspace is a subfunctor, hence its inclusion $i$ is a monomorphism; therefore $\alpha\beta=\mathrm{id}_W$. This proves the canonical isomorphism $B\simeq W$ and both projection compatibilities. Its composite with $i$ is the asserted closed immersion $c$.

proof.text: Let $U=T\setminus V(\mathcal K)$. The blowup chart-properties node identifies $T^{\prime}\times_TU$ with $U$. On this open the exceptional equation is a unit, so a section killed by its power is zero and $\mathcal H$ restricts to zero. Hence $W\times_TU=P\times_TU=Y\times_TU$, with its projection to $T^{\prime}\times_TU=U$ equal to the restriction of $g$.

If $T$ is qcqs, the blowup chart-properties node says $p:T^{\prime}\to T$ is proper, hence quasi-compact and separated. The quasi-compactness convention in the cited locality node, tested on the quasi-compact space $T\to T$, gives quasi-compactness of $T^{\prime}$. The quasi-separated calculus makes $p$ quasi-separated, and the quasi-separated-source node, applied to $p$ and the quasi-separated target $T$, makes $T^{\prime}$ quasi-separated. No finite-presentation hypothesis is used.

If $g$ is separated and of finite type, its base change $P\to T^{\prime}$ is separated by the separation/base-change node and of finite type by the finite-type calculus (whose last clauses identify its stack and ordinary algebraic-space notions). The closed immersion $i:W\hookrightarrow P$ is proper by the closed-subspace-proper node, so in particular separated and of finite type. Composition gives that $W\to T^{\prime}$ is separated and of finite type. Finally every separated algebraic-space morphism is quasi-separated by the quasi-separated calculus, which is exactly the required quasi-compactness of its relative diagonal.
